study type: multicenter, randomized, and controlled clinical trial
outcome: upper and lower respiratory tract infections
signs and symptoms of dyspeptic syndromes
gut microbiota composition (alpha-biodiversity, relative abundance of Bacteroidota, Actinomycetota, Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, B. bifidum, Escherichia/Shigella, and Haemophilus)
cohort: 164 newborns born by cesarean section (intervention) and 249 untreated newborns (control)
finding: 6 months of B. bifidum supplementation in children born by cesarean section reduced the risk of gut dysbiosis and had a positive clinical impact that remained observable in the following 6 months of follow-up.
mod_finding: B. bifidum supplementation in children born by cesarean section reduced the risk of gut dysbiosis and had a positive clinical impact.
